The operstate of a device is initially IF_OPER_UNKNOWN and is updated
asynchronously by linkwatch after each change of carrier state
reported by the driver.  The default carrier state of a net device is
on
column2: and this will never be changed on drivers that do not support

For devices that do support carrier detection
carrier state to off initially
column2: then poll the hardware state when the

column1: device is opened.  However

column1: unregistered device
column2: and commit b473001 ('net: Do not fire linkwatch

column1: events until the device is registered.') ensured that we don't.  But
this means that the operstate for many devices that support carrier
detection remains IF_OPER_UNKNOWN when it should be IF_OPER_DOWN.
The same issue exists with the dormant state.
The proper initialisation sequence
column2: avoiding a race with opening of

column1: the device
rtnl_lock();
rc = register_netdevice(dev);
if (rc)
goto out_unlock;
netif_carrier_off(dev); /* or netif_dormant_on(dev) */
rtnl_unlock();
but it seems silly that this should have to be repeated in so many
drivers.  Further
column2: the operstate seen immediately after opening the

column1: device may still be IF_OPER_UNKNOWN due to the asynchronous nature of
linkwatch.

to fix this by setting the operstate synchronously
reverted as it could lead to deadlock.

only.
